statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 17 (low), Stress 49 (elevated), Confidence 86 (high). One narrow window is flagged around the quarterly expiration close.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with the mapped EA_ON state for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, because the session's retracements are completing rather than failing. A narrow flagged window covers 19:00-20:15 UTC, where the mapped forecast state moves to WATCH around the quadruple-witching close auction. Tail remains below the block threshold throughout, and standing existing-position management and emergency protection are unchanged.
headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces its morning dip in full ahead of the quarterly expiration close
body: NDX trades at 29,484 (+0.13%) inside a 0.64% session band of 29,372-29,560 after opening at 29,529, selling off to the low and recovering the entire move, so retracements are completing rather than failing and no persistent one-way structure is present. VIX is 15.24 within a 14.99-15.63 range and shows no bid for protection. The macro backdrop stays demanding: the Federal Reserve raised its target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September and its projections point to a further hike by year-end, the 10-year Treasury yield holds 5.00% against a 2-year at 4.74%, and crude remains above $100 with Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline still impaired after the 10-11 September drone strikes. WTI eased 1.8% to $100.06 today, which marginally relieves the energy-to-yields channel without resolving it. This combination is scored as elevated Stress rather than Tail, consistent with the rule that event importance and cross-asset tension raise drawdown risk before they establish a no-retracement path. Today's August industrial production release was soft, with total output unchanged and manufacturing down 0.3%, and it did not move the index out of its band. Today is the September quadruple-witching expiration, which concentrates unwind and rebalance flow into the 20:00Z cash close; the flagged window covers that auction and its immediate aftermath. CME equity-index futures then close for the week at 21:00Z, so twenty-one of the twenty-four forecast hours carry no tradable price path and Tail falls to a residual weekend floor that represents Sunday reopen gap exposure.

lookbackSummary: The Thursday afternoon that followed the 16 September Fed hike carried a trend-up mode and Tail of 20-21, mapping to WATCH through 21:00Z. Tail decayed to 17-18 overnight as the mode normalised, then held between 15 and 19 across the Asian and European sessions with the mapped state at EA_ON. The mode shifted from trend-up to mixed at 11:00Z as the US morning turned two-way, and it has stayed mixed since. Stress climbed from the low 40s to around 50 on crude above $100 and the 10-year pressing 5%, easing only marginally as oil pulled back today. All 24 lookback hours are covered by published assessments.
outlookSummary: The remaining US afternoon is expected to stay inside its band under expiration pinning, with the narrow flagged window at 19:00-20:15 UTC covering the quadruple-witching close auction and its unwind, where forecast Tail peaks at 21 and the mapped state is WATCH. CME equity-index futures then close for the week at 21:00Z, so the final twenty-one hours of the window carry no tradable price path; forecast Tail settles at a residual 11-13 and drifts up slowly as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates toward the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, which falls outside this window. Confidence decays from 86 to 72 across the halt because no fresh price-path evidence can arrive. The unresolved Saudi East-West pipeline outage and the signalled further Fed tightening are the stored conditionals for Monday, whose first calendar item is the 12:30Z Chicago Fed activity index.
